asked_by: Madhav, 26 Oct 2026 12:19 Toronto: "lets fix everything. i say yes to your recommendations" (the recommendation: test support and resistance as an ENTRY signal; until now only swing-low exits and the retest cards were tested)
title: Support and resistance as an entry: does a bounce off support or a close through resistance give a buy call (and a close below support a sell call)?
hypothesis: Buying a stock that touches its swing-low support and closes up within 1.5% above it, or that closes above its swing-high resistance, beats ordinary days over the next 20 sessions (and pays after costs); a close below support is followed by weaker returns; the same bounce and breakout on the Nifty and Bank Nifty are followed by better index returns.

data.index: silver/kite_index/day (NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK) 2003-2023, closes only, via india.teachers_stock.index_panel (rows before 2024 only)
data.stocks: gold/teachers/stock_panel.parquet (adjusted daily bars of the liquid universe, to 2023-12-29); events and base = liquidity rank 1-250 that day
data.nothing_sealed: no 2024+ row and no sealed folder is read

definitions.swing point (the technicals panel's own: a swing low is a bar whose low is the lowest of the 5 bars on each side; a swing high, whose high is the highest. It is known only 5 sessions after the bar (no look-ahead). Index: closes stand in for highs and lows, as in the live panel
definitions.support S_w / resistance R_w, as of the: among swing points whose bar lies in the last w sessions before today (w = 20 or 60; the panel uses 60) and that are confirmed by yesterday: S = the highest swing low below yesterday's close, R = the lowest swing high above yesterday's close
definitions.bounce_w (stocks): today's low <= S_w x 1.01 (touched), today's close between S_w and S_w x 1.015, and today's close above yesterday's close; one event per stock per 10 sessions
definitions.break_w (stocks): today's close above R_w (R_w was above yesterday's close, so this is the first close above it); one per 10 sessions
definitions.breakdown60 (stocks): today's close below S_60 (the first close below the support); one per 10 sessions
definitions.bounce60 / break60 (index): bounce: yesterday's close <= S_60 x 1.01 (touched), today's close up and between S_60 and S_60 x 1.015; break: today's close above R_60; one per 10 sessions
definitions.segments (stocks): swing points and levels use only the stock's continuous run of sessions in the panel (no level carried across a gap)

outcomes.index: from the next session's close to the close 20 sessions later: fwd20
outcomes.stocks: buy at the next open, sell at the close 20 sessions later, net of the delivery round trip and the spread estimate (india/costs.py): net20

statistics.index (market timing): india.teachers_stock.msplit against all other sessions with levels defined, quarter blocks, Welch t
statistics.stocks vs ordinary days: india.teachers_stock.level: event mean minus the mean of all base rows (every 5th session of every liquid-250 stock, plus the events) in the same quarter, t across quarters
statistics.stocks, the trade itself after costs: india.teachers_stock.absolute: the event's own mean net20, quarter means
statistics.verdict: india/registry.record standard rule; MIN_DATES 16 blocks per period

bar.note: family 'technical' (XO1's 27 variants) plus these 11; k frozen at 38
